newsitem.title: FINLAND: Metra, Fincantieri diesel units to merge.
newsitem.headline: Metra, Fincantieri diesel units to merge.

text.p: Finnish engineering group Metra Oy Ab said in a statement on Thursday that it had tentatively agreed to merge its Wartsila Diesel unit with Italian Fincantieri's diesel engine activities.
The new company will be a part of Metra, and Fincantieri will have up to 15 percent holding in the merged company, Metra said.
"The new company to be formed though this merger will be the largest in its field worldwide," Metra said.

-- Wartsila Diesel, a leading maker of medium-speed diesel engines and a big supplier of high-speed engines for marine vessels and power plants with 1995 net sales of 6.92 billion markka and 6,100 employes;
-- Swiss New Sulzer Diesel, a maker of slow- and medium-speed diesel engines for marine applications and power plants with 1995 net sales of 672 million Swiss francs and 1,175 employees;
-- Diesel Ricerche S.p.A., a research and development company with 1995 net sales of 28 billion Italian lira and 176 employees;

-- initially a 40 percent participation in Grandi Motori, Fincantieri's engineering division, a maker of slow- and medium-speed diesel engines with 1995 net sales of 426 billion lira and 1,700 employees.
"The parties aim to finalise the agreements requires for the completion of the transaction by the end of the year," Metra said.

"The actual size of Fincantieri's shareholdig and Metra's cash payment ... will be based on the values of the business operations being contributed and the related financing arrangements," Metra said. It did not elaborate.

New Sulzer Diesel is now 50 percent owned by Fincantieri, which also has the right to buy the remaining half from German Vulkan Industrie Holding GmbH, which is controlled by the bankruptcy estate of Bremer Vulkan Verbund AG.
